english.title: Disclose information regarding manufacturing process / trade secret obtained when entering land
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having entered land, in exercise of a right of entry conferred under or by virtue of section 196A or 196B of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, disclosed to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) information obtained by you while on the land as to a

(A)_[manufacturing process]_
(B)_[trade secret]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 196C(5) and (7) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
entered land in exercise of a right of entry
disclosed to a person
information obtained while on the land as to a manufacturing process/trade secret

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 196C(6) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 provides that section 196C(5) does not apply if the disclosure is made by a person in the course of performing his duty in connection with the purpose for which he was authorised to enter the land.

other.penalty:
Summary: Statutory maximum fine.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
